translation_en:
Second Session
Discourse
“The Sage-King Becomes the People's Ruler and Teacher”
Lin Mi

Comment by Associate Examiner Qu, Instructor: 〔The topic itself is lofty and dignified, and candidates find it easy to compose essays on it; yet their thousand-odd words are generally so superficial and diffuse as to become tiresome. This essay grounds its argument in the topic and does not pursue verbal ornament. Its〕〔opening and closing movements, its restraint and emphasis, all strike precisely at the essential points. Surely this is writing that penetrates inward and applies to oneself! I record it as a model for those who indulge in verbal〕〔display.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Professor: 〔The sage-king rules and teaches the countless multitudes; possessing both virtue and position, he undertakes their education and nourishment together. This is a proposition unchanging through ten thousand generations. You have developed it into a coherent essay, with ideas appearing in successive〕〔layers, and your language is lofty and antique. Can such writing be found among the examination essays of our day? As the finest work of this session, it truly〕〔deserves recommendation for a high ranking.〕

Comment by Examiner Mo, Instructor: 〔The argument is incisive and pertinent, and merits acceptance.〕

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔Pure in expression and grand in spirit: an outstanding discourse.〕

The sage is one who bears Heaven's charge. Turning back to his own person, he finds that the virtue of all under Heaven resides in himself, and that whereby he orders…

title: 嘉靖二十二年河南鄉試錄
text:
綸天下者其本敦寄之以位則天下之權在我
而所以宰制天下者其勢順故其始也以其身
先天下而立極之道可以神運而不窮出其道
也以天下之所有而導天下之人則綏猷之化
可以四達而不悖嗚呼此聖人所以承天意理
人羣而納軌物之要道也朱子曰聖王作民君
師其此之謂歟且天下之生久矣洪荒之世淳
風未開毛茹而血飲相安於榛榛狉狉之俗而
不識不知惟曰帝力何有於我而已中古以還
===
汤穆日漓智慧日長其所以相生相養有非復
作息食飲之舊焉者而世道始紛紛然矣不有
以治之其孰從而遂之不有以覺之其孰從而
復之古耶斯民也即上古之民也其羣然而生
者未始不秩然而敘也由相臨有君臣之倫焉
由相親有父子之倫焉由相合有夫婦之倫焉
由相聯有昆弟之倫焉由相與有朋友之倫焉
是道也天之經也人之紀也出於人心之本然
而古與今之所弗異也自夫理以氣拘性以情
punctuated: 綸天下者，其本敦；寄之以位，則天下之權在我，而所以宰制天下者，其勢順。故其始也，以其身先天下，而立極之道可以神運而不窮；出其道也，以天下之所有而導天下之人，則綏猷之化可以四達而不悖。嗚呼！此聖人所以承天意、理人羣而納軌物之要道也。朱子曰：「聖王作民君師。」其此之謂歟？且天下之生久矣，洪荒之世，淳風未開，毛茹而血飲，相安於榛榛狉狉之俗，而不識不知，惟曰：「帝力何有於我？」而已。中古以還，汤穆日漓，智慧日長，其所以相生相養，有非復作息食飲之舊焉者，而世道始紛紛然矣。不有以治之，其孰從而遂之？不有以覺之，其孰從而復之古耶？斯民也，即上古之民也；其羣然而生者，未始不秩然而敘也。由相臨，有君臣之倫焉；由相親，有父子之倫焉；由相合，有夫婦之倫焉；由相聯，有昆弟之倫焉；由相與，有朋友之倫焉。是道也，天之經也，人之紀也，出於人心之本然，而古與今之所弗異也。自夫理以氣拘，性以情
translation_en:
…the foundation for ordering all under Heaven is firm. Entrusted with office, he holds the authority of all under Heaven, and his position enables him to govern it with ease. Thus, at the outset, he leads all under Heaven by his own example, and the Way by which he establishes the supreme standard can operate with wondrous efficacy, without exhaustion. In bringing forth his Way [?], he draws upon what exists throughout the world to guide its people; the transforming influence by which he brings order to their ways can then reach in all four directions without deviation. Ah! This is the essential Way by which the sage accords with Heaven’s intent, orders human society, and brings people within proper norms. Master Zhu said, “The sage king becomes the people’s ruler and teacher.” Was this not what he meant?

Human life under Heaven has indeed endured for a long time. In the primeval age, before simple customs had developed, people ate flesh with its hair and drank blood. They lived contentedly together amid wild vegetation and beasts, without knowledge or awareness, saying only, “What does the sovereign’s power have to do with me?” Since middle antiquity, harmony [?] has daily grown thinner, while intelligence has daily increased. The means by which people sustain and nourish one another have ceased to follow the old patterns of work and rest, eating and drinking, and the ways of the world have begun to fall into confusion. Unless someone governs them, who will guide them toward fulfillment? Unless someone awakens them, who will guide them back to antiquity?

These people are the very same as the people of high antiquity. In living together as a multitude, they have never lacked an orderly arrangement. From relations of authority arises the bond between ruler and minister; from affection, the bond between father and son; from union, the bond between husband and wife; from familial connection, the bond between elder and younger brothers; and from association, the bond between friends. This Way is Heaven’s constant norm and humanity’s ordering principle. It issues from the original constitution of the human heart and is no different in ancient times and today. Once principle is constrained by material force, and human nature by feelings…

title: 嘉靖二十二年河南鄉試錄
text:
蕩心以物遷其初始於不親不遜而其流至於
相欺相軋相殘而無所底止此非天之所能及
也代天工而賛化育不有待其人而行者乎是
故天將降大任於是人也必先與之以任之之
資焉賦之德矣而不重之以權則不尊而天下
不信重以權矣而不敦厚其德則無本而天下
不從故天將委以經世之責者必聖人在天子
之位而後可也書曰天降下民作之君作之師
天果無意於聖人乎蓋惟聖人作民之君也則
===
行其師道以率天下而其權始尊惟聖人作民
之師也則出其君道以臨天下而其本斯豫此
聖人所以承天之責而必兼君師之任也惟王
盡制惟聖盡倫盡制其君之道乎盡倫其師之
道乎夫道一而已倫與制非二物也自其本之
於身而建天下之皇極則盡倫自其措之於業
而秩天下之大猷則盡制制即倫之所爲也此
天之委聖人所以必兼德與位而聖人所以副
天之托者必盡倫與制而後君師之道全也是
punctuated: 蕩，心以物遷，其初始於不親不遜，而其流至於相欺相軋相殘，而無所底止。此非天之所能及也。代天工而賛化育，不有待其人而行者乎？是故天將降大任於是人也，必先與之以任之之資焉。賦之德矣，而不重之以權，則不尊而天下不信；重以權矣，而不敦厚其德，則無本而天下不從。故天將委以經世之責者，必聖人在天子之位而後可也。《書》曰：「天降下民，作之君，作之師。」天果無意於聖人乎？蓋惟聖人作民之君也，則行其師道以率天下，而其權始尊；惟聖人作民之師也，則出其君道以臨天下，而其本斯豫。此聖人所以承天之責而必兼君師之任也。「惟王盡制，惟聖盡倫。」盡制，其君之道乎？盡倫，其師之道乎？夫道一而已，倫與制非二物也。自其本之於身而建天下之皇極，則盡倫；自其措之於業而秩天下之大猷，則盡制。制即倫之所爲也。此天之委聖人所以必兼德與位，而聖人所以副天之托者，必盡倫與制，而後君師之道全也。是
translation_en: …is unsettled, and the heart is swayed by external things. At first this begins with a lack of affection and deference; its consequences extend to mutual deception, oppression, and violence, without any limit. This is beyond what Heaven itself can accomplish. Does carrying out Heaven’s work on its behalf and assisting its transforming and nurturing activity not depend upon the right person to act? Thus, when Heaven is about to confer a great charge upon such a person, it must first grant him the capacities needed to bear it. If it endows him with virtue but does not add the weight of authority, he will lack honor and all under Heaven will not trust him. If it gives him the weight of authority but does not deepen his virtue, he will lack a foundation and all under Heaven will not follow him. Thus, when Heaven entrusts someone with responsibility for ordering the world, only a sage occupying the position of the Son of Heaven will suffice. The Book of Documents says: “Heaven brought forth the people below and established rulers for them and teachers for them.” Can Heaven truly have no intention concerning the sage? Only when the sage serves as the people’s ruler does he practice the way of the teacher to lead all under Heaven, and only then is his authority honored. Only when the sage serves as the people’s teacher does he bring forth the way of the ruler to preside over all under Heaven, and thus his foundation is made ready. This is why the sage, in accepting Heaven’s charge, must combine the responsibilities of ruler and teacher. “Only the king fully realizes institutions; only the sage fully realizes human relationships.” Is fully realizing institutions not his way as ruler? Is fully realizing human relationships not his way as teacher? The Way is one, and human relationships and institutions are not two separate things. Insofar as he roots it in his own person and establishes the supreme standard for all under Heaven, he fully realizes human relationships. Insofar as he puts it into practice in his undertakings and gives order to the great principles governing all under Heaven, he fully realizes institutions. Institutions are precisely the expression of human relationships. This is why Heaven’s commission to the sage requires that he possess both virtue and position, and why the sage, in fulfilling Heaven’s trust, must fully realize both human relationships and institutions. Only then is the way of ruler and teacher complete. Thus…

title: 嘉靖二十二年河南鄉試錄
text:
故聖王之於天下也治之而爭奪息矣導之而
生養遂矣不有以敎之則胥人道以羣鳥獸非
所以承天之意而盡綏猷之責也聖人有憂之
必欲舉一世而甄陶之而其心始釋然耳故其
始也必以其身先於天下而典自我敦禮自我
庸自宮闈以及於朝廷篤父子之親正君臣之
位理陰陽之敎敦行葦之仁章顯比之道蓋明
昭至德以臨照風勵乎臣民者無弗盡其道焉
則天下之人極立矣此聖人以身敎天下也猶
===
以爲未可以齊也于是制之以太學有上下庠
之設也有東西序之立左右學之建也又有爲
瞽宗爲東膠爲虞庠爲辟廱成均者矣而又以
時臨之所以身親天下之敎也乃於是推其制
以及於天下羣之學校聯之師儒綜之以黨庠
術序比之以左塾右塾參之以先路次路而又
有州長黨正以糾攷之上老庶老以臨率之里
胥鄰長以綜理之所以廣勵學官之路也又于
是著之話言予之法制陳之藝極定之章程委
punctuated:
故聖王之於天下也，治之而爭奪息矣，導之而生養遂矣。不有以敎之，則胥人道以羣鳥獸，非所以承天之意而盡綏猷之責也。聖人有憂之，必欲舉一世而甄陶之，而其心始釋然耳。故其始也，必以其身先於天下，而典自我敦，禮自我庸。自宮闈以及於朝廷，篤父子之親，正君臣之位，理陰陽之敎，敦行葦之仁，章顯比之道。蓋明昭至德，以臨照風勵乎臣民者，無弗盡其道焉，則天下之人極立矣。此聖人以身敎天下也。
猶以爲未可以齊也，於是制之以太學，有上下庠之設也，有東西序之立、左右學之建也，又有爲瞽宗、爲東膠、爲虞庠、爲辟廱、成均者矣。而又以時臨之，所以身親天下之敎也。乃於是推其制以及於天下，羣之學校，聯之師儒，綜之以黨庠術序，比之以左塾右塾，參之以先路次路，而又有州長黨正以糾攷之，上老庶老以臨率之，里胥鄰長以綜理之，所以廣勵學官之路也。又於是著之話言，予之法制，陳之藝極，定之章程，委
translation_en:
…Thus, in their dealings with all under Heaven, sage kings govern them so that contention and strife cease, and guide them so that life and nurture flourish. Unless they also instruct them, however, they bring humanity down to the company of birds and beasts. This would not fulfill Heaven’s intention or discharge their responsibility to establish an orderly way of life. The sage worries about this and can find peace of mind only by molding and cultivating an entire generation. Thus, at the outset, he must personally set an example for all under Heaven: established norms are strengthened through him, and ritual is put into practice through him. From the palace’s inner quarters to the court, he deepens affection between father and son, rectifies the positions of ruler and minister, orders instruction concerning yin and yang, strengthens the benevolence expressed in “Reeds Along the Path” (Xing wei), and makes manifest the way of “manifest union” (xian bi). In making his consummate virtue shine forth to illuminate, influence, and encourage officials and people, he leaves no aspect of the Way unfulfilled. Thereby the supreme standard for humanity is established throughout the realm. This is how the sage teaches all under Heaven through his own person.
Yet he still considers this insufficient to bring everyone into accord. Accordingly, he establishes institutions centered on the Imperial University: upper and lower xiang schools are established, eastern and western xu schools instituted, and left and right schools built. There are also institutions called the Guzong, Dongjiao, Yuxiang, Biyong, and Chengjun. He visits them at appropriate times, personally attending to the education of all under Heaven. He then extends this system throughout the realm, gathering people into schools and linking them through teachers and classical scholars. He coordinates them through district xiang and local xu schools, arranges them through the left and right village schools, and supplements them with the xianlu and cilu [?]. There are also township heads and district heads to inspect and assess them, senior elders and other elders to oversee and lead them, and village officers and neighborhood heads to coordinate their affairs. This broadens the avenues for encouraging educational officials [?]. He then sets these matters forth in instructive sayings, provides laws and regulations, lays out standards for the arts of learning, establishes rules and procedures, and entrusts…

title: 嘉靖二十二年河南鄉試錄
text:
之常秩所以廣敎也而命簡其不帥敎不變者
移之屛之以至終身不齒所以糾惡以示戒也
然猶懼其弗若於訓也於是乎又制爲之刑以
弼之齊八政以防之又所以輔敎之所不及而
善其道於無窮也夫聖人之於天下帥之以身
廣之以學條之以制長之以人而又輔之以刑
如此乎其詳且備也而要其所爲敎者脩六禮
明七敎不越乎君臣父子夫婦昆弟朋友之間
而孰非天下之所固有者乎聖人亦因其所有
===
而品之節之鼓舞而振德之使天下各循其所
有以還乎其初耳是故聖人之於天下也道之
而弗牽順之而弗咈而天下涵濡於聖人之敎
也景從而谷應風行而海流而明倫之化天下
大同矣此聖人所以財成天地之道輔相天地
之宜以左右民必如是而後君師之道無負於
天之責也嗚呼古之聖人若堯之恊和也舜之
愼㣲也禹之敷文命也湯之脩人紀也武之建
皇極也是數聖人者當繼天立極之會爲制法
punctuated:
之常秩，所以廣敎也。而命簡其不帥敎、不變者，移之、屛之，以至終身不齒，所以糾惡以示戒也。然猶懼其弗若於訓也，於是乎又制爲之刑以弼之，齊八政以防之，又所以輔敎之所不及而善其道於無窮也。夫聖人之於天下，帥之以身，廣之以學，條之以制，長之以人，而又輔之以刑，如此乎其詳且備也！而要其所爲敎者，脩六禮，明七敎，不越乎君臣、父子、夫婦、昆弟、朋友之間，而孰非天下之所固有者乎？聖人亦因其所有而品之、節之，鼓舞而振德之，使天下各循其所有以還乎其初耳。是故聖人之於天下也，道之而弗牽，順之而弗咈，而天下涵濡於聖人之敎也，景從而谷應，風行而海流，而明倫之化，天下大同矣。此聖人所以財成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，以左右民，必如是而後君師之道無負於天之責也。
嗚呼！古之聖人，若堯之恊和也，舜之愼㣲也，禹之敷文命也，湯之脩人紀也，武之建皇極也，是數聖人者，當繼天立極之會，爲制法
translation_en:
…to regular offices: this was how instruction was extended. They also ordered that those who would neither follow instruction nor reform be singled out, relocated, and expelled, even to the point of lifelong exclusion from recognized standing. This was how wrongdoing was corrected and a warning given. Yet they still feared that people would not comply with their instruction. Accordingly, they also established punishments to support it and coordinated the eight affairs of government to prevent wrongdoing. These measures supplemented what instruction could not reach and perfected their way for all time. In dealing with all under Heaven, the sages led by personal example, extended instruction through schools, gave it order through regulations, appointed people to lead, and further supported it with punishments. How detailed and comprehensive their arrangements were! Yet the essentials of their instruction—cultivating the six rites and clarifying the seven teachings—did not extend beyond the relationships between ruler and minister, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger brothers, and friends. Which of these was not already inherent in all under Heaven? The sages simply worked with what people already possessed, distinguishing its proper degrees and regulating it, inspiring them and stirring their virtue, so that everyone under Heaven might follow what they inherently possessed and return to their original condition.
Thus, in dealing with all under Heaven, the sages guided without dragging and followed people's dispositions without thwarting them. Immersed in the sages' instruction, people followed like shadows and responded like echoes in a valley; its influence moved like the wind and flowed like the sea. Through the transforming influence of clarified human relationships, all under Heaven attained Great Unity. This is how the sages shaped and completed the Way of Heaven and Earth, assisted what was fitting to Heaven and Earth, and thereby aided the people. Only in this way could the Way of the ruler and teacher fulfill the responsibility entrusted by Heaven.
Ah! Among the sages of antiquity, Yao brought harmony; Shun attended carefully to the subtlest matters; Yu spread his civilizing commands; Tang cultivated the bonds of human relationships; and Wu established the Supreme Standard. These sages, at the juncture when they succeeded Heaven and established the ultimate standard, instituted laws …

title: 嘉靖二十二年河南鄉試錄
text:
興王之君而德位兼隆倫制並舉盡君師之道
以終代天之功而時雍風動之休平成表正之
績永清垂拱之治天地以位萬物以育其萬世
君師之極者乎是故聖人君師之道又所以贊
天地之所不及而與之參焉者也嗚呼此聖人
之所以有功於天地也
表
擬宋以韓琦范仲淹爲樞密副使謝表慶
曆三年
===
曹金
同考試官教諭陳　批〔氣溫詞雅得臣子對揚之體〕
篇終慷慨激勵有規無諂韓范立朝大節溢然言
表矣
同考試官教諭李　批〔引用精當音節和平宜錄以式〕
考試官教諭莫　批〔典則中有藻麗〕
考試官教諭張　批〔是長于四六者〕
慶曆三年月日伏蒙
聖恩命臣琦臣仲淹爲樞密副使謹上
punctuated:
興王之君，而德位兼隆，倫制並舉，盡君師之道，以終代天之功，而時雍風動之休，平成表正之績，永清垂拱之治，天地以位，萬物以育，其萬世君師之極者乎？是故聖人君師之道，又所以贊天地之所不及，而與之參焉者也。嗚呼！此聖人之所以有功於天地也。

表

擬宋以韓琦范仲淹爲樞密副使謝表，慶曆三年。

曹金

同考試官教諭陳，批〔氣溫詞雅，得臣子對揚之體〕篇終慷慨激勵，有規無諂，韓范立朝大節，溢然言表矣。

同考試官教諭李，批〔引用精當，音節和平，宜錄以式〕

考試官教諭莫，批〔典則中有藻麗〕

考試官教諭張，批〔是長于四六者〕

慶曆三年月日，伏蒙聖恩，命臣琦、臣仲淹爲樞密副使，謹上
translation_en:
…sovereigns who brought royal rule to flourishing, whose virtue and position were alike exalted, and who established both human relationships and institutions. They fulfilled the Way of ruler and teacher, completing their work on Heaven’s behalf. Through the blessings of universal harmony and transforming influence, the achievements of bringing order to the land and setting upright examples, and the government that secured lasting peace while the ruler sat with folded hands, Heaven and Earth took their proper places and all things were nurtured. Were these not the supreme exemplars of rulers and teachers for all ages? Thus the sage’s Way as ruler and teacher also supplements what Heaven and Earth cannot accomplish, making him a third power alongside them. Ah! This is how the sage renders service to Heaven and Earth.

Memorial

A memorial of thanks, composed in the persons of Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan upon their appointment as Vice Commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs under the Song, in the third year of Qingli [1043].

By Cao Jin.

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: 〔The tone is gentle and the diction elegant, fitting the manner in which a subject acknowledges and extols imperial favor.〕 The conclusion is impassioned and stirring, offering admonition without flattery. The great integrity that Han and Fan displayed at court shines forth beyond the words themselves.

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔The allusions are precise and appropriate, and the rhythm harmonious and balanced. It should be recorded as a model.〕

Examiner Mo, Instructor, comments: 〔Within its adherence to classical standards, there is ornamental beauty.〕

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔This writer excels in four-and-six parallel prose.〕

On this day of this month in the third year of Qingli, we, your servants Qi and Zhongyan, have humbly received your sagely favor appointing us Vice Commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and respectfully submit…

title: 嘉靖二十二年河南鄉試錄
text:
表稱
謝者伏以
鴻樞密勿切瑶極之清華卿案明揚次鈞
衡而峻陟官雖列于陪貳
恩已極于章縫聯絲綍以同升顧
寵光而交愧〔臣〕等誠惶誠恐稽首頓首上言
竊惟安危注意于將相資
廟筭之萬全出納惟允于樞機接台辰之三曜
虎符專典忝帷幄以運籌龍節遥分統韜
鈐而禦侮入則叙百揆之重帝載咸熙出
則張九伐之威王猷允塞風人矢詠吉甫
隆業于中興太史策勛子儀挺生于再造
蓋才必兼乎文武故任可屬以腹心若非
長子之貞曷稱价人之選茲蓋伏遇
===
○○○○
至仁享帝
峻德配天
統乾元以時乘
punctuated:
表稱謝者。伏以鴻樞密勿，切瑶極之清華；卿案明揚，次鈞衡而峻陟。官雖列于陪貳，恩已極于章縫。聯絲綍以同升，顧寵光而交愧。〔臣〕等誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首上言。
竊惟安危注意于將相，資廟筭之萬全；出納惟允于樞機，接台辰之三曜。虎符專典，忝帷幄以運籌；龍節遥分，統韜鈐而禦侮。入則叙百揆之重，帝載咸熙；出則張九伐之威，王猷允塞。風人矢詠，吉甫隆業于中興；太史策勛，子儀挺生于再造。蓋才必兼乎文武，故任可屬以腹心。若非長子之貞，曷稱价人之選？茲蓋伏遇○○○○，至仁享帝，峻德配天，統乾元以時乘……
translation_en:
…submit this memorial to express our thanks. We humbly consider that diligent service in the great Bureau of Military Affairs brings one close to the pure splendor of the imperial seat; selection and advancement among the high ministers [?] raise one to an exalted position immediately below the chief councillors. Although our offices rank only among the deputies, the favor bestowed upon us has reached the utmost that scholars in their ceremonial caps could receive. Joined in the imperial decree and promoted together, we look upon this glorious favor with shared embarrassment. We, your servants, in utmost fear and trepidation, bow our heads to the ground and submit these words.
We reflect that the security or peril of the realm directs attention to its generals and chief councillors, upon whom the court relies for infallible strategic planning. Faithful transmission of commands and reports rests with the pivotal offices, which stand beside the three luminaries of the highest ministers. Entrusted exclusively with the tiger tallies of military command, we are unworthily admitted to the command tent to devise strategy; dispatched afar with dragon-decorated credentials, we direct military affairs and repel aggression. At court, we put the weighty affairs of the many offices in order, so that the sovereign’s undertakings may all flourish; in the field, we display the might of the nine forms of punitive expedition, so that the royal way may prevail everywhere. The poets proclaimed in song how Jifu achieved great deeds in an age of restoration; the Grand Astrologer recorded the merits of Ziyi, who arose to rebuild the dynasty. Since ability must encompass both civil and military affairs, these responsibilities can be entrusted only to intimate and trusted ministers. Without the steadfastness of the eldest son, how could one merit selection as a great and worthy man?
This is because we have humbly encountered Your Majesty—○○○○—whose utmost benevolence offers fitting sacrifice to the Lord on High, whose lofty virtue matches Heaven, and who commands the primal creative power of Heaven, mounting it at the proper times …

title: 嘉靖二十二年河南鄉試錄
text:
假豐亨而宜照六卿分治仰
聖人之無爲一怒安民識仁者之有勇邇以獷
夷革面狼燧息煙謂忘戰之則危乃用人
而惟舊本兵副職猥及書生肴府崇階謬
充下質〔臣琦臣仲淹〕瞻卿雲之五色一芥
躬逢竝厲蠻于四賢孤忠自許嘗聞俎豆
無柳渾之知兵徒讀父書愧謝安之料敵
班先鵷列才匪鷹揚矧腹背之毛思扶摇
而罔力顧玄黄之乘希沃若以中疲連茹
===
以征何幸占其泰運積薪取誚無乃累于
離明沾翚渥以知榮翔金華而自分愓若棟
撓之懼深惟餗覆之愆敢不揹七尺以折
衝庶幾效寸長于牧圉幸揀掄于哲匠可
云柱石無能叨剪紼于神工不覺騰驤有
意屹長城之萬里臣何有焉見多壘于四
郊心之憂矣伏願
因時講武戢干戈以事農
思患預防聽鼓鼙而任將欽降王于河隴柔
punctuated:
假豐亨而宜照，六卿分治，仰聖人之無爲；一怒安民，識仁者之有勇。邇以獷夷革面，狼燧息煙，謂忘戰之則危，乃用人而惟舊。本兵副職，猥及書生；肴府崇階，謬充下質。〔臣琦臣仲淹〕瞻卿雲之五色，一芥躬逢；竝厲蠻于四賢，孤忠自許。嘗聞俎豆，無柳渾之知兵；徒讀父書，愧謝安之料敵。班先鵷列，才匪鷹揚。矧腹背之毛，思扶摇而罔力；顧玄黄之乘，希沃若以中疲。連茹以征，何幸占其泰運；積薪取誚，無乃累于離明。沾翚渥以知榮，翔金華而自分。愓若棟撓之懼，深惟餗覆之愆。敢不揹七尺以折衝，庶幾效寸長于牧圉。幸揀掄于哲匠，可云柱石無能；叨剪紼于神工，不覺騰驤有意。屹長城之萬里，臣何有焉；見多壘于四郊，心之憂矣。
伏願因時講武，戢干戈以事農；思患預防，聽鼓鼙而任將；欽降王于河隴，柔
translation_en:
…attaining abundance and prosperity and appropriately shedding light. The Six Ministers divide the work of government, looking up to the sage’s effortless rule; with a single display of wrath you bring peace to the people, showing that the benevolent possess courage. Recently the fierce foreigners have changed their outward demeanor, and the wolf-dung beacon fires have ceased to smoke. Yet, judging that forgetting warfare brings danger, you have employed men long known to you. The deputy post in charge of military affairs has undeservedly fallen to mere scholars; the exalted rank of the “Yao Office” [?] has mistakenly been filled by men of inferior worth. 〔Your servants Qi and Zhongyan〕 Gaze upon the five-colored auspicious clouds: insignificant as mustard seeds, we have personally encountered this blessing. Together we would strive alongside the four worthies [?], pledging our single-hearted loyalty. We have learned something of sacrificial vessels and ritual, but lack Liu Hun’s knowledge of warfare; we have merely read our fathers’ books and stand ashamed before Xie An’s ability to assess the enemy. Our precedence places us ahead of the ranks of courtiers, but our talents lack the soaring prowess of hawks. Moreover, like feathers on a bird’s belly and back, we wish to ride the whirlwind but have no strength; like horses exhausted and discolored, we hope to remain sleek and vigorous, yet tire midway. Advancing together like uprooted grasses whose roots intertwine, how fortunate we are to encounter an age of flourishing! Yet, inviting the reproach that newly piled firewood is placed above the old, might we not compromise your discerning brilliance? Bathed in abundant favor [?], we recognize our honor; soaring at Jinhua, we nevertheless know our proper measure. We tremble at the danger of the roof beam bending and ponder deeply the fault of overturning the cauldron’s food. How could we fail to devote our seven-foot bodies to repelling attack, hoping to contribute even our meager abilities among the herdsmen and grooms? Fortunately selected by a wise master builder, can we claim to lack the capacity to serve as pillars and foundation stones? Favored by the divine craftsman’s cutting of our tethers [?], we find ourselves aspiring to gallop and leap. To stand firm as a Great Wall of ten thousand li—what capacity have your servants for that? To see enemy ramparts multiplying in the four outskirts—this fills our hearts with sorrow.
We humbly wish that you would practice military exercises at the proper seasons, then lay aside shields and spears so that the people may farm; anticipate troubles and take precautions, choosing commanders as you hear the drums of war; reverently receive surrendered kings in the He–Long region [?], and conciliate …

title: 嘉靖二十二年河南鄉試錄
text:
重譯于要荒璇璣齊七政而氛祲消干羽
舞兩階而聲教訖
廣輪縻極拓禹跡之輿圖
天位龍飛偃周波于瀚海臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
===
第叁場
策五道
第一問
曹金
同考試官教諭陳　批〔我〕
朝典憲酙酌古今蓋至我
皇上而後明備皆時之不容已也子能於一篇中三致意焉非泛然呫嗶之學者髙薦宜也
同考試官教諭李　批〔制度有本有文我〕
國家制度蓋先本後文由內及外以抵於聖神功化之極所謂兼本末合內外以收夫全體
punctuated:
重譯于要荒，璇璣齊七政而氛祲消，干羽舞兩階而聲教訖。廣輪縻極，拓禹跡之輿圖；天位龍飛，偃周波于瀚海。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叁場
策五道
第一問
曹金
同考試官教諭陳批〔我〕朝典憲，酙酌古今，蓋至我皇上而後明備，皆時之不容已也。子能於一篇中三致意焉，非泛然呫嗶之學者，髙薦宜也。
同考試官教諭李批〔制度有本有文，我〕國家制度，蓋先本後文，由內及外，以抵於聖神功化之極，所謂兼本末、合內外，以收夫全體
translation_en:
…through successive interpreters in the remotest regions. When the jeweled astronomical instrument brings the Seven Regulators into alignment, baleful vapors disappear; when shields and feather plumes are danced between the two stairways, imperial renown and instruction reach everywhere. Extend dominion to the utmost breadth and length [?], enlarging the mapped realm traced by Yu; ascending dragonlike to the heavenly throne, spread Zhou’s pacifying influence to the Vast Sea [?]. We, your servants, look toward Heaven and revere Your Majesty with the utmost fervor and trembling awe. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our thanks and bring them to Your Majesty’s hearing.
Third Session
Five Policy Questions
First Question
Cao Jin
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: 〔Our〕 dynasty’s statutes and ordinances draw judiciously upon both antiquity and the present. Only under our present Emperor have they become fully articulated and complete; all were indispensable responses to their times. That you emphasize this three times within a single essay shows that you are no mere student of superficial recitation. Your recommendation for a high place is fitting.
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔Institutions have both foundations and outward forms. Our〕 state’s institutions give precedence to foundations and then to outward forms, proceeding from the inner to the outer, thereby attaining the utmost achievement of sagely and inspired transformation. This is what is meant by embracing both root and branches, uniting the inner and outer, in order to realize the complete substance …

title: 嘉靖二十二年河南鄉試錄
text:
大用之功者此篇所陳庶幾得之
考試官教諭莫　批〔以鄉校儒生而於〕
昭代故實敷荅無遺足占所養矣
考試官教諭張　批〔因革損益粲然如指諸掌蓋〕
長於贊
聖德之形容者
理有不容以不一者聖人經制之大法理
有不得以盡同者聖人彌綸之妙用甚矣
制作聖人能事也經制於前者所以立大
中之本彌綸於後者所以適通變之宜一
===
天理之公而已聖人何嘗容心哉是故經
制違之天下彌綸通於無窮此創造者貴
緣物以立極因事以昭則而繼承者當通
其變不膠其故師其意不泥其迹貽謀裕
后之規克纂前脩之美諒無以易此矣洪
惟我
太祖高皇帝以聰明睿知之聖垂中正仁義之
統驅胡元之亂嚴華夷之防制禮作樂建
punctuated:
大用之功者，此篇所陳庶幾得之。
考試官教諭莫批〔以鄉校儒生而於〕昭代故實敷荅無遺，足占所養矣。
考試官教諭張批〔因革損益，粲然如指諸掌，蓋〕長於贊聖德之形容者。
理有不容以不一者，聖人經制之大法；理有不得以盡同者，聖人彌綸之妙用。甚矣，制作聖人能事也！經制於前者，所以立大中之本；彌綸於後者，所以適通變之宜：一天理之公而已，聖人何嘗容心哉？是故經制違之天下，彌綸通於無窮。此創造者貴緣物以立極，因事以昭則，而繼承者當通其變，不膠其故，師其意，不泥其迹。貽謀裕后之規，克纂前脩之美，諒無以易此矣。洪惟我太祖高皇帝，以聰明睿知之聖，垂中正仁義之統，驅胡元之亂，嚴華夷之防，制禮作樂，建
translation_en:
…the achievement of full efficacy: what this essay sets forth comes close to attaining it.
Examiner Mo, Instructor, comments: 〔As a Confucian student of a local school,〕 he gives a comprehensive account of the precedents of this illustrious dynasty, omitting nothing. This is sufficient to reveal the learning he has cultivated.
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔Continuities and changes, reductions and additions, are presented as clearly as though pointing to things in one’s palm. He is evidently〕 accomplished at depicting and praising the imperial virtue.
Where principle permits no lack of unity, there lie the great rules by which sages establish institutions; where principle cannot allow complete uniformity, there lies the wondrous operation by which sages comprehensively order affairs. How great it is: the creation of institutions is the distinctive accomplishment of sages! Establishing institutions at the outset lays the foundation of the great Mean; comprehensively ordering affairs thereafter achieves what is fitting through adaptation to change. All is simply the impartiality of Heaven’s principle. When have sages ever imposed private intentions upon it? Thus institutional ordering extends throughout the realm [?], while comprehensive ordering reaches without limit. Those who create institutions must therefore attend to things in establishing the supreme standard and respond to affairs in making the rules manifest. Those who inherit them must accommodate their changes without clinging to old arrangements, emulate their intent without being bound by their outward traces. Surely nothing can replace this as the rule for bequeathing plans that enrich posterity and successfully carrying forward the excellence of worthy predecessors.
We reverently reflect that our Taizu, the Exalted Emperor, with the sage’s keen perception and profound wisdom, handed down a tradition of centrality, correctness, benevolence, and righteousness. He swept away the disorder of the non-Chinese Yuan, strictly maintained the distinction between Chinese and non-Chinese peoples, instituted rites, created music, and established…

title: 嘉靖二十二年河南鄉試錄
text:
制立法纖悉委曲罔不畢備固足以俟后
聖而不惑矣
列聖相承益隆繼述治化洋溢協氣流通美矣
盛矣然而參酌古今會稡典制則無踰於
大明會典一書焉其開局纂輯一以諸司職掌
為主類以
祖訓等書附以見行事例大綱旣正萬目畢舉
大明中天誠有目所共仰者也請舉其大者揄
揚於萬一可乎惟始
聖祖稽古定制斟酌會通可以謂之無遺矣然
中歲晚年間有續定者如置大宗正院掌
玉牒也初領以
親王繼改為府而以勳戚掌之置中書省總
政務也初領以左右丞相繼革其官而以
六部分理之去樞密之職總其政于兵部
革行省之名統其事于藩臬兵以振國威
也罷諸翼而設督府分督府而為五府統
外衛于都司隸都司于諸府其他一事一
punctuated:
制立法，纖悉委曲，罔不畢備，固足以俟后聖而不惑矣。列聖相承，益隆繼述，治化洋溢，協氣流通，美矣盛矣！然而參酌古今，會稡典制，則無踰於《大明會典》一書焉。其開局纂輯，一以《諸司職掌》為主，類以《祖訓》等書，附以見行事例，大綱旣正，萬目畢舉。大明中天，誠有目所共仰者也。請舉其大者，揄揚於萬一，可乎？
惟始聖祖稽古定制，斟酌會通，可以謂之無遺矣。然中歲晚年，間有續定者。如置大宗正院，掌玉牒也，初領以親王，繼改為府，而以勳戚掌之；置中書省，總政務也，初領以左右丞相，繼革其官，而以六部分理之；去樞密之職，總其政于兵部；革行省之名，統其事于藩臬。兵以振國威也，罷諸翼而設督府，分督府而為五府，統外衛于都司，隸都司于諸府。其他一事一
translation_en:
…institutions and enacted laws, providing fully for every minute detail and intricate circumstance. These were assuredly sufficient to await a later sage without misgiving. Successive sage emperors inherited his work, increasingly enriching and carrying it forward. Orderly government and moral transformation spread abundantly, and harmonious influences circulated everywhere. How admirable and flourishing! Yet for weighing ancient and present practices together and compiling institutional regulations, nothing surpasses the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming (Da Ming huidian). When a bureau was established to compile it, the Duties of the Various Offices (Zhusi zhizhang) served throughout as its principal basis; materials from the Ancestral Injunctions (Zuxun) and other books were arranged by category, and currently operative precedents were appended. With its main framework correctly established, every detailed provision was included. The Great Ming stands like the sun at its zenith, truly admired by all who have eyes to see. May I cite its principal features and thus praise even a ten-thousandth part of its achievements?
At the beginning, the sagely founder examined antiquity and established institutions, weighing precedents and adapting them into a coherent whole. One might say that he omitted nothing. Nevertheless, in the middle and later years of his reign, further provisions were occasionally established. For example, he created the Court of the Imperial Clan to keep the imperial genealogies, initially placing an imperial prince at its head. Subsequently he reorganized it as the Imperial Clan Court and entrusted it to meritorious nobles and imperial relatives. He established the Secretariat to oversee governmental affairs, initially placing the chief councilors of the left and right at its head. Subsequently he abolished those offices and divided their responsibilities among the Six Ministries. He eliminated the Bureau of Military Affairs and consolidated its functions under the Ministry of War. He abolished the designation of Branch Secretariat and placed its affairs under the provincial administration and surveillance commissions. Military forces served to display the state's might: he abolished the various wings and established the Chief Military Commission, then divided that commission into five commissions. He placed the guards outside the capital under the Regional Military Commissions and subordinated those regional commissions to the five chief commissions. As for every other affair and every…

title: 嘉靖二十二年河南鄉試錄
text:
物綜理周密正
朝廷以正百官正百官以正萬民
聖祖精神心術之微雖不可得而聞其可聞者
寧不在玆乎
聖子
神孫丕承洪業然事與時移政由俗革亦後世
守成者之不容已也是故在
成祖文皇帝則以置諸司于
行在嬀于南北並建官制于是乎有損益矣
達漕運于北都因而疏渠濬淮水利于是
===
乎有變易矣在
仁宗昭皇帝則
郊祭尊
太祖
成祖以配天
廟享合文武功臣以竝配在
宣宗章皇帝則革交趾之一道中國不混于夷
設屯田之專官兵食自裕于用在
punctuated:
物，綜理周密，正朝廷以正百官，正百官以正萬民。聖祖精神心術之微，雖不可得而聞，其可聞者寧不在玆乎？

聖子神孫丕承洪業，然事與時移，政由俗革，亦後世守成者之不容已也。是故在成祖文皇帝，則以置諸司于行在，嬀于南北並建，官制于是乎有損益矣；達漕運于北都，因而疏渠濬淮，水利于是乎有變易矣。在仁宗昭皇帝，則郊祭尊太祖、成祖以配天，廟享合文武功臣以竝配。在宣宗章皇帝，則革交趾之一道，中國不混于夷；設屯田之專官，兵食自裕于用。在
translation_en:
…things were comprehensively and meticulously administered. By rectifying the court, he rectified the hundred officials; by rectifying the hundred officials, he rectified the myriad people. Although the subtle workings of the sacred founder’s spirit and mind cannot be learned of, surely what can be known of them lies here?

His sagely sons and divine grandsons grandly inherited his vast undertaking. Yet affairs shift with the times, and government changes with prevailing customs: these, too, are adjustments that later rulers preserving the established achievement cannot avoid. Thus, under Emperor Chengzu Wen, the establishment of offices at the temporary imperial seat, with parallel establishments in the south and north [?], brought additions and reductions to the official system. Extending grain transport to the northern capital, and consequently dredging canals and deepening the Huai River, brought changes to water management. Under Emperor Renzong Zhao, Taizu and Chengzu were honored as associated recipients of sacrifices to Heaven at the suburban sacrifices, while civil and military meritorious officials were brought together as associated recipients of offerings in the ancestral temple. Under Emperor Xuanzong Zhang, the abolition of the Jiaozhi administrative region kept China from being mingled with the non-Chinese peoples; the appointment of officials specifically responsible for military agricultural colonies ensured ample grain for the army’s needs. Under …

title: 嘉靖二十二年河南鄉試錄
text:
英宗睿皇帝則立團營而督以重臣塵河道而
理以憲職在
憲宗純皇帝則復軍運之舊例而民力紓設理
河之府職而責成備在
孝宗敬皇帝則崇孝養而定
親王表賀之儀嚴報本而有
寢殿祧廟之建
列聖精神心術之微雖不可得言而其可言者
又不在於玆乎夫作於前者至精而至密
===
述於後者盡善而盡美即乎人心之安合
乎天理之正雖其因革損益間有異同
列聖之心一
皇祖之心也孰能出其範圍之神耶彼周禮一
書文質監于二代其法非不備也唐之六
典損益出于一時其文非不詳也其視我
朝之制散之汗青則星〔垂〕〔日〕麗藏之
秘府則圖見龜呈信非前世之所能及也然
行之旣久其勢有不得盡合者將不有待
punctuated: 英宗睿皇帝則立團營而督以重臣，塵河道而理以憲職。在憲宗純皇帝，則復軍運之舊例而民力紓，設理河之府職而責成備。在孝宗敬皇帝，則崇孝養而定親王表賀之儀，嚴報本而有寢殿祧廟之建。列聖精神心術之微，雖不可得言，而其可言者，又不在於玆乎？夫作於前者至精而至密，述於後者盡善而盡美，即乎人心之安，合乎天理之正。雖其因革損益間有異同，列聖之心，一皇祖之心也。孰能出其範圍之神耶？彼《周禮》一書，文質監于二代，其法非不備也；唐之《六典》，損益出于一時，其文非不詳也。其視我朝之制，散之汗青則星〔垂〕〔日〕麗，藏之秘府則圖見龜呈，信非前世之所能及也。然行之旣久，其勢有不得盡合者，將不有待
translation_en:
…Under Emperor Yingzong Rui, combined training camps were established and placed under the supervision of senior ministers; the river courses were [?] and administered by officials of the Censorate. Under Emperor Xianzong Chun, the old practice of military transport was restored, easing the burden on the people’s labor, and prefectural posts for river administration were established, making full provision for assigning responsibility for results. Under Emperor Xiaozong Jing, filial care was exalted and the ceremonial rules for princes’ congratulatory memorials were fixed; reverent repayment of ancestral beneficence was upheld through the construction of ancestral sleeping halls and temples for remote ancestors.

Although the subtle workings of the successive sage emperors’ spirits and minds cannot be put into words, are not these precisely the things about them that can be expressed? What was created by their predecessors was supremely refined and meticulous; what was carried forward by their successors was wholly good and beautiful, according with what brings peace to the human heart and conforming to the correctness of Heaven’s principle. Although their retention, alteration, reduction, and expansion of institutions sometimes differed, the minds of the successive sage emperors were one with the mind of the imperial ancestor. Who could surpass the wondrous scope of his ordering?

The Rites of Zhou took the balance of refinement and simplicity from the two preceding dynasties as its guide, and its regulations were certainly comprehensive. The Six Statutes of the Tang embodied reductions and additions made within a single age, and its text was certainly detailed. Yet consider our dynasty’s institutions: spread across the historical record, they shine like hanging stars and the radiant sun; preserved in the palace archives, they are like the revelation of the River Chart and the appearance of the auspicious tortoise. Truly, preceding ages could not match them. Yet, after they have been practiced for so long, circumstances inevitably arise in which they cannot fit completely. Must they not therefore await…

title: 嘉靖二十二年河南鄉試錄
text:
於
今日耶肆我
皇上紹履慶基恢弘大運遠追
聖祖之心法近紹
列聖之制度錯綜斟酌兼總條貫雲行雨施盡
舉曠世之典日臨月照獨觀萬化之原蓋
集
羣聖之大成立一王之昭憲者也自今觀之
九五有齋恭默有室
===
郊社兆南北之位日月定朝夕之儀肇
圓丘以祀
天而尊
祖之禮備開
明堂以享
帝而
嚴父之義昭其他如復
躬耕之典正孔子之祀
神機運用不一而足禮以義起政與時宜皆所
punctuated: 於今日耶？肆我皇上紹履慶基，恢弘大運，遠追聖祖之心法，近紹列聖之制度，錯綜斟酌，兼總條貫，雲行雨施，盡舉曠世之典；日臨月照，獨觀萬化之原。蓋集羣聖之大成，立一王之昭憲者也。自今觀之，九五有齋，恭默有室，郊社兆南北之位，日月定朝夕之儀。肇圓丘以祀天，而尊祖之禮備；開明堂以享帝，而嚴父之義昭。其他如復躬耕之典，正孔子之祀，神機運用，不一而足。禮以義起，政與時宜，皆所
translation_en:
… until the present day? Thus Our Emperor has succeeded to the auspicious foundation and enlarged the great imperial destiny. Looking far back, he follows the principles of the Sagely Ancestor’s mind; looking to more recent times, he carries forward the institutions of the successive sage emperors. He coordinates and weighs them, comprehensively ordering their guiding principles and particulars. Like moving clouds and falling rain, he puts into practice all the ceremonies neglected for ages; like the illuminating sun and moon, he alone perceives the source of the myriad transformations. He has indeed brought together the achievements of all the sages and established the manifest statutes of a sovereign.

Viewed from the present, the occupant of the sovereign’s seat has a hall for ritual purification and a chamber for reverent silence. Sites for the suburban sacrifices and the altars of soil have been marked out in the south and north, and the rites for the sun and moon have been fixed for morning and evening. He inaugurated the Round Mound for sacrifices to Heaven, thereby completing the rites for honoring the ancestor; he opened the Hall of Light for offerings to the Supreme Lord, thereby making manifest the principle of revering one’s father. Other measures include restoring the ceremony of personally plowing the field and rectifying the sacrifices to Kongzi. The workings of his sagely discernment are too numerous to enumerate. Ritual arises from what is right, and government accords with the needs of the time; all these are means by which …

title: 嘉靖二十二年河南鄉試錄
text:
以擴
列聖所未盡而會
聖祖所欲爲者矣亦何嘗容心於其間哉故其
奎章
天藻暉映寰區將與天地相爲終始豈特一代
制作已耶詩曰貽厥孫謀以燕翼子
聖祖之謂也傳曰聖人不凝滯於物而能與世
推移
列聖之謂也易曰通其變使民不倦神而化之
===
使民宜之
今上之謂也愚何幸躬逢其盛
第二問
孫觀
同考試官教諭曲　批　帝王禮樂之善良由至德爲之
本我
朝之禮樂所以追跡虞廷豈偶然哉子能鋪張殆盡而歸我
皇上脩道之言可謂達禮樂之本者歟
同考試官教授李　批　慕古樂而述我
punctuated:
以擴列聖所未盡，而會聖祖所欲爲者矣，亦何嘗容心於其間哉？故其奎章天藻，暉映寰區，將與天地相爲終始，豈特一代制作已耶？《詩》曰：「貽厥孫謀，以燕翼子。」聖祖之謂也。傳曰：「聖人不凝滯於物，而能與世推移。」列聖之謂也。《易》曰：「通其變，使民不倦；神而化之，使民宜之。」今上之謂也。愚何幸躬逢其盛！

第二問

孫觀

同考試官教諭曲批：帝王禮樂之善，良由至德爲之本。我朝之禮樂，所以追跡虞廷，豈偶然哉？子能鋪張殆盡，而歸我皇上脩道之言，可謂達禮樂之本者歟！

同考試官教授李批：慕古樂，而述我
translation_en:
…thereby extending what the successive sage emperors had left incomplete and fulfilling what the sagely founding ancestor wished to accomplish. When did he ever allow personal intent to intrude upon these undertakings? Thus his imperial writings and splendid compositions illuminate the realm and will endure as long as Heaven and Earth. Could they be merely the institutions and ordinances of a single dynasty? The Book of Odes says: “He bequeathed plans to his descendants, thereby securing and aiding his children.” This speaks of the sagely founding ancestor. A transmitted text says: “The sage does not remain bound to things but can move with the times.” This speaks of the successive sage emperors. The Book of Changes says: “Adapt through change, so that the people do not grow weary; transform with spiritual efficacy, so that the people find it fitting.” This speaks of His Majesty the present emperor. How fortunate I, in my humble capacity, am to witness this flourishing age in person!

Second Question

Sun Guan

Comment by Associate Examiner Qu, Instructor: The excellence of the rites and music of emperors and kings truly derives from consummate virtue as their foundation. Is it mere chance that our dynasty’s rites and music follow in the footsteps of the court of Yu [Shun]? You have expounded them almost exhaustively and concluded with words concerning our emperor’s cultivation of the Way. You may indeed be said to understand the foundation of rites and music!
